```{r, echo = FALSE}
bfcolor <- function(x, color) {
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    sprintf("(\textcolor{%s}{\textbf{%s}})", color, x)
  } else if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
    sprintf("<span style='color: %s;'><b>%s</b></span>", color, x)
  } else x
}
```

# Welcome to Data Wrangling! 🚗📊

We will learn about Data Wrangling and tidyverse's data science ecosystem through a real-world dataset about driving safety across US states from ["Dear Mona, Which State Has The Worst Drivers?"](https://web.archive.org/web/20260301023213/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/which-state-has-the-worst-drivers/)

## Objective

- Practice data wrangling, plotting and interpreting data by 
    - Completing the plots from lecture your turn
    - Recreating at least two plots from the article

# Part 1: Setting Up Your R Environment 

## Loading Required Packages

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)  # Data science toolkit (includes ggplot2, dplyr, readr, etc.)
library(kableExtra) # Pretty tables
```

## Import the data

```{r import-data}
# Import data directly from FiveThirtyEight's GitHub
#drivers <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fivethirtyeight/data/master/bad-drivers/bad-drivers.csv")

drivers <- read_csv("./data/bad-drivers.csv")
```

# Part 3: Exercises

Recall: `ggplot2` uses a "grammar of graphics" - you build plots layer by layer.

**Basic ggplot2 syntax:**
```r
ggplot(data = <DATA>) + 
  <GEOM_FUNCTION>(mapping = aes(<MAPPINGS>))
```
